Standard: The hydraulic and pneumatic filtration systems will maintain a particulate contamination level that complies with the air vehicle specifications for system cleanliness during flight, ground, and filling operations. If no cleanliness level is specified, the hydraulic filtration system will maintain a particulate contamination level of Class 8 (or cleaner) IAW SAE AS4059G, Contamination Levels paragraph and Maximum Contamination Limits for Differential Particle Counts (particles/100 mL) table, or Class 5 (or cleaner) IAW NAVAIR 01- 1A-17, Hydraulic Fluid Contamination chapter and Navy Standard for Particulate Contamination table. The level of water in each hydraulic system is less than 250 parts per million. The level of chlorine is less than 100 parts per million. The levels of other contaminants are defined and meet the requirements of the air vehicle specification. Filters are fully qualified or obtained from a QPL of prior approved filters against a military specification (e.g., MIL-DTL-8815) and meet requirements for the air vehicle system in terms of pressure drop and flow rate through the filter assembly. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Review QPL to verify that the filter element has been fully qualified.
(2) Inspect documentation such as system design specifications and industry specifications to verify that contamination (e.g., particulate, chlorine, water, and barium) levels are defined and documented.
(3) Inspect hydraulic ground cart system specifications to verify that the cart’s filtering capability meets the required air vehicle minimum cleanliness level. Test.
  (1) Lab test: For unqualified parts or parts not on the QPL, conduct lab testing to verify that the filter is qualified to QPL specifications.
  (2) Lab test: Conduct HITL (e.g., iron bird) testing to verify that filtration system performance (e.g., pressure drop, flow rate, and cleanliness) meets air vehicle requirements during static and dynamic system operation.
  (3) Ground test: Conduct on air vehicle testing to verify that filtration system performance (e.g., pressure drop and flow rate) meets air vehicle requirements during static and dynamic system operation. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (4) Flight test: Conduct fluid sampling on each system prior to flight test to establish a baseline cleanliness level and sample each system after first 20 hours of flight test to verify the system(s) maintains the required cleanliness level.
